Request rate fell from 40 requests/second (10:30-10:31 buckets) to 10 requests/second (10:32-10:34 buckets), so the latency increase coincides with lower, not higher, request volume.
Pool utilization was 0.6-0.7 for version v1 through the 10:31 bucket, then 1.0 (fully occupied) for version v2 from the 10:32 bucket onward, coinciding with the latency increase.
Trace discovery returned one slow checkout trace (id 00000000000000000000000000000001, ~1060 ms) at 2026-09-19T10:33:10Z, consistent with the degraded window; no span-level breakdown was retrieved.

leading_hypothesis.statement: The checkout latency increase beginning around the 10:32 bucket coincides with a version change from v1 to v2 and with the connection pool becoming fully utilized (ratio 1.0), while request rate simultaneously dropped. This pattern is consistent with connection pool saturation (e.g., a smaller effective pool or a leak introduced with v2) causing requests to wait on connections rather than with a load-driven slowdown. The mechanism (connection wait) is inferred, not directly measured.

supporting_findings.statement: Mean checkout latency rose roughly 5x, from ~0.21-0.22s in the 10:30-10:31 buckets to ~1.04-1.08s in the 10:32-10:34 buckets.
The latency increase coincided with a 4x drop in request rate (40 to 10 requests/second), ruling out a simple request-volume surge as the explanation.

Pool utilization reached 1.0 (fully occupied) in every degraded bucket under version v2, versus 0.6-0.7 under v1, and the utilization label change from v1 to v2 coincides with the latency onset bucket.
Trace discovery found at least one ~1060 ms checkout request at 10:33:10Z, matching the elevated latency window, though it is a limited match, not a population average.

contradicting_findings.statement: Full pool utilization alone does not prove saturation is the cause, and no connection-wait metric or wait span was collected to confirm the mechanism.

The v1-to-v2 label change in pool_utilization suggests a version change, but a lingering version gauge or label change alone does not prove a deployment caused the behavior, and no configuration (pool_limit) evidence was collected to compare versions.
